root_cause.text: In `net/bluetooth/hci_sync.c`, `hci_adv_bcast_annoucement()` failed to validate that prepending Broadcast Announcement service data to an existing advertising instance’s `adv_data` would fit in the fixed temporary buffer `ad`, allowing an oversized extended advertising payload to overflow the rebuild buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (adv->adv_data_len > sizeof(ad) - len) { bt_dev_err(hdev, "No room for Broadcast Announcement"); return -EINVAL; }` immediately before `memcpy(ad + len, adv->adv_data, adv->adv_data_len);`, and the CVE description says existing advertising instances can already hold the maximum extended advertising payload so the combined data “may no longer fit in the temporary buffer used to rebuild the advertising data.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check to prevent overflow when building broadcast announcement advertising data.
intent_record.what: After appending Broadcast ID service data to the advertisement buffer, a new length check was added to verify that adv->adv_data_len fits in the remaining space of the local ad buffer; if it does not, the code logs "No room for Broadcast Announcement" and returns -EINVAL before the memcpy.
intent_record.how: This prevents copying advertising payload data past the end of the ad buffer when constructing a broadcast announcement, avoiding buffer overflow and aborting the operation cleanly if there is insufficient space.

grouping_result.intent: Add a bounds check to prevent overflow when building broadcast announcement advertising data.

candidates.rationale: This copies the existing advertising payload into the fixed-size temporary buffer `ad` without any prior bounds check against `len + adv->adv_data_len`, which is the direct overflow point described in the root cause.

This uses the potentially oversized combined length when rebuilding the advertising instance, reflecting the same missing validation that allows an oversized payload to be accepted and written past the temporary buffer.

In this commit, the buffer was enlarged to `u8 ad[HCI_MAX_EXT_AD_LENGTH];`, and the code now appends the existing advertising payload with `memcpy(ad + len, adv->adv_data, adv->adv_data_len);` before calling `hci_set_adv_instance_data(..., len + adv->adv_data_len, ad, ...)`. This means the function explicitly preserves and reuses existing `adv_data` while building the new payload, which is the relevant logic for the vulnerability. However, the fix path is already present because the code now uses the maximum extended advertising length buffer and reconstructs the combined payload instead of the old fixed `ad[4 + 3]` size that caused the overflow.
